{{Top}}
{{Citation}}
{{Quote|People wonder why Jedi are forbidden to marry or have families. They don't see how attachments always lead to suffering.|Jedi Master [[Orgus Din]], on the drawbacks of marriage and the inevitable, unbalancing consequence of attachment|<ref name="Star Wars: The Old Republic">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Mara_Wedding_Dress.jpg|thumb|right|220px|[[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]] preparing for her 
[[Wedding of Luke Skywalker and Mara Jade|wedding]] to [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]]]
'''Marriage''' was the official union of two beings, usually a union of mutual love and attraction. However, in some cases, the union was for [[Politics/Legends|political]] reasons. Marriage could sometimes produce offspring, depending on cultural mandates, personal choice, or lack thereof.

==Description==
{{Quote|The marriage is arranged, of course&mdash;we're not commoners.|[[Fume Pachoola]]|<ref name="Hondo Ohnaka's Not-So-Big Score">{{InsiderCite|144|Hondo Ohnaka's Not-So-Big Score}}</ref>}}
Within many [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] societies, marriage choices were in most cases made through courtship.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> Across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], a myriad of wedding traditions existed amongst the different [[Species/Legends|species]], most of which were generally of a monogamous nature. However, some species, such as the [[Cerean/Legends|Cereans]], due to either their culture or even reproductive rates, advocated [[Polygamy|polygamous]] unions.

==History==
{{Quote|And what Leia doesn't know, I don't know. That's the secret to a happy marriage, actually.|[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]|<ref name="Fate of the Jedi: Conviction">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Conviction]]''</ref>}}
Under the original order, Jedi were forbidden to marry because they believed attachment could lead an individual to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]], as was the case with [[Shaela Nuur]]. Despite the ban and the associated dangers, many Jedi, including [[Kento Marek]], [[Ranik Solusar]], [[Nejaa Halcyon]], [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], wed, either in secrecy or with the knowledge and disapproval of the Jedi Council. Normally this led to disciplinary actions being taken against them, however, in the case of Halcyon and Skywalker the Order seemed to close its eyes to it.<ref name="The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref><ref name="Obsession 2">[[Obsession 2|''Obsession'' 2]]</ref> These unions often resulted in children, who themselves became Jedi.

Due to the low ratio of [[Gender/Legends|males]] to females amongst [[Cerean/Legends|Cereans]], [[Ki-Adi-Mundi/Legends|Ki-Adi-Mundi's]] was granted an exception to Jedi rules on marriage.<ref name="SW1">[[Star Wars (1998) 1|''Star Wars'' (1998) 1]]</ref> Ultimately, and he was allowed to marry five women (with whom he fathered seven children). [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Siri Tachi/Legends|Siri Tachi]] fell in love, but chose to separate and remain true to the [[Jedi Code/Legends|Jedi Code]], while [[T'ra Saa/Legends|T'ra Saa]] and [[Tholme/Legends|Tholme]] entered a clandestine relationship but never married. [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]] chose to leave the Jedi Order to be with his wife [[Khaleen Hentz/Legends|Khaleen Hentz]] and son [[Korto Vos]], though the Republic fell before he could act on his decision.

The [[New Jedi Order]] a different policy on marriage from the old Order; under the leadership of [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], the Jedi were allowed to marry and Skywalker himself married [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]].
[[File:OronGaliaBinding.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A royal [[Onderon/Legends|Onderonian]] wedding, one of many marriage rituals]]

Some species, such as the [[Zeltron/Legends|Zeltron]], were devoted to the pursuit of pleasure and upheld hedonistic values, and marriage was not held in high regard. Some Zeltrons made an attempt to "educate" others on the "errors of monogamy." There were Zeltrons who thought differently, but they were rare. [[Deliah Blue]] was in a monogamous relationship with [[Cade Skywalker]] in [[137 ABY]], and even felt jealousy, a near unheard of emotion for a Zeltron to feel.

Inter-species marriages were rare, though not unheard of, and sometimes produced offspring. Commonly, such unions were between a Human and a near-Human, as in the case of the [[Lethagoe]], although more exotic unions were present, such as [[Cut Lawquane/Legends|Cut Lawquane's]] marriage with his [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] wife, [[Suu Lawquane/Legends|Suu]]. However, it was unlikely that such pairings would produce [[Hybrid/Legends|hybrid]] children, in the absence of genetic modification or even [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith alchemy]]. Jedi Master [[Arca Jeth]] had [[Sephi/Legends|Sephi]] ancestry, and [[Darth Malgus]] had a relationship with a Twi'lek, [[Eleena Daru]], although they never married. This move echoed the history of the Sith, where members of the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith species]] would [[Sith Empire/Legends|interbreed]] with the [[Exiles]]. These unions produced many powerful Sith Lords who were strong in the power of the dark side. [[Marka Ragnos]] and [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]] were two examples of such beings. Another exotic example of cross-species mating would be the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] assassin [[Aurra Sing/Legends|Aurra Sing]], the offspring of a Human mother and a father of an unknown species, whom she had inherited certain traits from, most easily seen with her alabaster-white skin. In other cases, offspring of unions between Humans and near-Humans were not so markedly different from the normal appearance of baseline Humans, although sometimes they did face certain cultural or clan issues, as in the case of the Human/[[Kiffar/Legends|Kiffar]] [[Hybrid/Legends|hybrid]] [[Ailyn Vel]].
